questions.answer: APIRouter is a mini-app with its own prefix/tags; main app mounts it via include_router. Enables per-feature files (users/router.py) and versioning (/v1, /v2).
questions.question: Why use APIRouter instead of putting all routes on one FastAPI app?

questions.answer: Middleware runs on every request automatically (logging, timing, CORS). Depends() runs only on routes that declare it (auth, paging, DB). Use middleware for cross-cutting, Depends for opt-in.
questions.question: Contrast middleware vs Depends() in FastAPI.

questions.answer: Short-lived access token (~15m) sent on every API call; long-lived refresh (~7d) used only at /refresh to mint new access. Limits damage if access leaks; refresh stored securely and sent rarely.
questions.question: Explain the access vs refresh token pattern.

questions.answer:
from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
users_router = APIRouter(prefix='/users', tags=['users'])
@users_router.get('')
def list_users():
    return [{'name': 'Kakade'}]
app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(users_router)

questions.answer: It expects form fields username/password (OAuth2PasswordRequestForm), not JSON. Sending JSON gives 422. Fix by sending form-data or using docs Authorize button.

questions.answer: BackgroundTasks has no retries or persistence; if the server crashes the email is lost. For critical/retried/scheduled work use Celery or APScheduler; BackgroundTasks is only fire-and-forget.
